name: AGILYSYS INC

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: That I am applying a cash-flow model to a company deliberately trading near-term cash for a recurring base worth far more, and that the market is right to look through it. Subscription revenue growing 34% with 66.6% recurring mix is the strongest operating evidence in this session's ten; the company is debt-free with $137.6M of cash and just raised guidance on every line. Software buyers pay on revenue and ARR, not on a reverse DCF, and 8.75x forward sales with a Rule-of-40 near 43 is inside the band comparable names trade at. A model that calls this 50%-plus overvalued is the same model that would have called every quality compounder overvalued for a decade.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Free cash flow re-accelerating in fiscal 2027 H2 and fiscal 2028 - specifically whether full-year FCF grows faster than the 17-18% revenue guide - and whether basic weighted-average shares stop rising.
devils_advocate.already_visible: The opposite is visible. Q2 free cash flow was $14.8M against $15.0M, flat against revenue up 17.7%, and the share count rose 1.0% while SBC rose 22%. Both of the counter's load-bearing assumptions - that cash follows revenue, and that compensation is paid for - are contradicted by this quarter's own numbers.
devils_advocate.unresolved: Whether an 8.75x forward revenue multiple is simply what this quality of asset costs, in which case the DCF is the wrong lens rather than the wrong number. I cannot close the gap between a +46% required growth rate and a multiple that peers would call ordinary, and that is why conviction is medium rather than high.

what_changed: Fiscal 2027 second-quarter results, 2026-10-26. Revenue $93.4M +17.7%; recurring $62.2M; subscription +32.6%; GAAP net income $13.2M ($0.46 diluted) against $11.7M ($0.41); adjusted diluted EPS $0.67 against $0.40. Full-year guidance raised to $374-378M of revenue, subscription growth to at least 34%, adjusted EBITDA to 25% of revenue. Cash $137.6M against $116.9M at fiscal year-end, no debt. The one number that did not improve is the one that decides the valuation: FREE CASH FLOW IN THE QUARTER WAS $14.8M AGAINST $15.0M A YEAR EARLIER - flat, while revenue grew 17.7%. Alongside that, share-based compensation for the six months was $12,281k against $10,029k, up 22%, and basic weighted-average shares ROSE to 28,142k from 27,882k in the quarter and 28,122k from 27,838k for the half.
consensus_case: Agilysys is a vertical SaaS compounder in hospitality - property management, point of sale, booking and golf software for hotels, casinos, cruise lines and resorts - and it is executing. Fiscal 2027 Q2 revenue was a record $93.4M, up 17.7%; subscription revenue grew 32.6% and recurring revenue is now 66.6% of the total; gross margin improved to 64.6% from 61.7%; and management RAISED full-year guidance to $374-378M of revenue with subscription growth of at least 34% and adjusted EBITDA at 25% of revenue. The business is debt-free with $137.6M of cash and a long runway: it is still converting an installed base off perpetual licences onto subscription, and each conversion raises revenue per property. At 8.75x forward revenue for a company compounding high-teens with a Rule-of-40 near 43, the market is paying a normal premium-SaaS multiple, not a bubble one.
base_case_rationale: I underwrite a genuinely good business growing revenue in the high teens with meaningful operating leverage still to come: adjusted EBITDA margin at 25% can plausibly reach the low-to-mid thirties as the subscription mix matures, so free cash flow should compound faster than revenue. Twenty per cent a year for five years takes an SBC-expensed base of $36M to roughly $90M on revenue near $750M - a 12% free-cash-flow margin rising to the high teens. That is a demanding but achievable path and it is well above the company's own guided revenue growth of 17-18%, which is the right place for a software business converting mix. I will not underwrite more than that, because the evidence this quarter runs the other way: free cash flow was flat on revenue up 17.7%, so the margin is compressing, not expanding, and the growth is currently being funded rather than harvested.
key_risks: Free cash flow was FLAT year over year in Q2 while revenue grew 17.7% - the cash margin is compressing as the business scales
Basic weighted-average shares rose 1.0% year over year while share-based compensation rose 22% to about $25M annualised: the compensation is not being paid for
At 8.75x forward revenue and about 35x guided adjusted EBITDA, there is no valuation support if growth decelerates even modestly
Hospitality technology spend is discretionary and cyclical; the installed base is hotels, casinos and cruise lines
watch_for: Full-year fiscal 2027 free cash flow against the 17-18% revenue growth guide - it must grow faster, and this quarter it did not grow at all
Basic weighted-average share count: a flat or falling count would move the base from $36M back toward $54M and cut the required growth by 12 points
Any sign that capitalised software development is absorbing the cash the income statement is reporting
